{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZVZPsg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhC8qmI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 23, "title": "Implement Saturn 16-bit CS0 transfers and SH7604 burst-ROM sequencing", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `e76cb2b8e3e9d0c44855d40ab94d026b644853f6`, `Bsc::bus_width` returns four bytes for CS0. Consequently, both SH-2s issue single-beat longword accesses in this region. Existing reset tests explicitly expect PC and SP vector reads to finish at clocks 8 and 16. These expectations preserve the model’s assumption rather than independently establish console behavior.

The [VA0.5 board drawing](https://consolemods.org/wiki/images/1/1b/Sega_saturn_va0.5_schematics.pdf), sheet 1, identifies MD4=0/MD3=1 on both processors and a word-output boot ROM. This is independent board documentation, not a Sega manual or emulator implementation. The [Hitachi SH7604 Hardware Manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/sh7604.pdf), §3.3/table 3.9, maps that strap to 16-bit CS0. Sections 7.3.1/figure 7.3 define transfer lanes; §7.8/figures 7.44–7.46 define BSTROM sequencing, including its zero-wait exception. Sections 7.11.1–7.11.2 cover reset boundaries, instruction fetches and cache fills.

`Bsc::access_timing` also gives every ordinary beat the same cost irrespective of BSTROM. Its existing test explains away burst-ROM behavior using the incorrect 32-bit adapter.

## Expected outcome

Implement fixed 16-bit CS0 behavior for the standard console on both processors, including ordinary transfers and the documented BSTROM read sequences. Route real scheduled transfers through the existing ownership, buffering and completion machinery.

Cover CS0 ROM and low-RAM accesses, instruction fetch/refill, CPU-local DMA and reset paths. Preserve narrower device contracts, SMPC byte accesses, backup odd-byte lanes, mirrors, ROM write protection and existing SCU prohibited-route checks. This task does not introduce configurable board variants or require electrical pin simulation.

## Context and reproduction

Read `src/onchip/bsc.rs:410–420,503–525`, `src/bus.rs:1176–1205`, `src/bus/transactions.rs:1260–1290` and `src/reset_tests.rs:22–40`. The width helper selects four-byte CS0 transfers; the reset test encodes their completion deadlines. `docs/architecture.md:441–445` explicitly records the assumption.

An uncontended ordinary longword under reset wait settings should have two word beats, completing at clocks 8 and 16 after grant. Cold PC/SP acquisition therefore requires four beats through clock 32. These are controlled bus-vector expectations, not measured console startup latency.

There are no open task Issues in the inspected repository state. Recent #19/#21 work supplies scheduled video/CD evidence but does not resolve this bus mismatch. Existing fixture reproduction succeeded for `build_sh2_reset_bus.py --check` and `build_bus_transactions.py --check`; Rust execution was not performed during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement fixed 16-bit CS0 selection for both SH-2s across construction, cold/system/watchdog resets and slave stop/start. BCR2 or CS1–CS3 memory settings must not change this strap. Preserve existing independently configurable non-CS0 widths.
- [ ] Add independently authored native vectors with literal addresses, widths, values and completion clocks for byte/word/long accesses, P1 aliases, aligned instruction fetches at both word positions, retained successor words and complete cache fills. Check partial sampling/publication by changing unsampled data between beats; debugger reads must not advance transfers.
- [ ] Implement and test BSTROM’s eligible read grouping, second-beat timing and zero-wait exception. Distinguish independent word requests from halves of one longword, restart groups correctly during cache fills and 16-byte DMA, and prevent stale burst state across cancellation or ownership changes. Derive expected traces from §7.8 rather than production timing helpers.
- [ ] Verify both CPU-local DMACs with CS0 longword and 16-byte transfers, retained data, count/address progress and completion IRQ ordering. Verify CPU buffered writes, peer contention, TAS exclusion and refresh interactions using legal routes. Preserve SCU access restrictions.
- [ ] Replace the inherited atomic-vector expectations with four separately sampled word phases. Cover cold boot, SSHON, external-BIOS SYSRES and both watchdog reset kinds. Assert no early PC/SP/instruction publication, peer progress, manual-reset draining, power-reset cancellation and absence of stale completion after a new boot selection. Exercise reset at each affected beat boundary.
- [ ] Execute an original MIT-licensed synthetic BIOS/SH-2 diagnostic in native Machine and rebuilt production Wasm. Both CPUs must perform actual ROM/low-RAM accesses and record computed payloads, FRT timing and synchronization results. Include changed payload/wait operands, repeated cold boots and an omitted-transfer control. Host code may load media and inspect results but must not synthesize guest computation.
- [ ] Demonstrate that a substantive new native or guest assertion fails against the inherited 32-bit implementation. Repeat board traces with advancement chunks 1, 3, 17 and 10000; preserve identical results and ordering. Do not substitute updated snapshots for independent expectations.
- [ ] Update architecture, conformance and validation records with exact specification references, implementation/test links, fixture hashes, actual results and remaining assumptions. Correct stale CS0/reset claims. Explain any changed historical timing assertion from a transfer trace; retain its substantive payload, IRQ and cancellation checks.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, all existing plus new fixture/media reproduction checks, and the complete extended `npm run test:browser` under `/saturn-rust/`. Preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, #19/#21 regressions, Canvas/audio, controllers, backup, input release and local-file privacy checks without required skips.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral semantics, full multiprocessor arbitration/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain outstanding. Passing this task establishes neither umbrella completion nor broad commercial-game compatibility. Tracker administration is outside this task.

## Optional validation

Additional independently documented board revisions may corroborate the fixed strap. Personal firmware, commercial discs, physical consoles, human approval and live Pages inspection are unnecessary.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
